function: Joint estimation of cascaded transmitting and reflecting channels of all users from noisy mixture pilots, extrapolating the full channel from N/Gamma sampled elements (pp. 1, 7).
system: Passive STAR-RIS (energy splitting, coupled phase shift), 8x64 elements in 4x32 sub-surfaces; AP 4x8 UPA; K=2 single-antenna UEs per group; 28 GHz; hardware impairments (pp. 4-6, 12).
method: Multi-task network (shared encoder, K task decoders, axial MLP, attention gating); supervised L1 loss with learnable uncertainty weights and ES-ratio prior; SGD (pp. 7-10, 12).
data_channel: Simulated hybrid-field clustered channel (near-field, visibility regions) following 3GPP TR 38.901 indoor mmWave framework and InH path loss; dataset size not stated (pp. 4, 12).
test_conditions: Trained with HWI level 0.1, tested at 0 to 0.2 (Fig. 14, p. 14); dataset size and training SNR not stated.
baselines: Classical: LS [23], CS-OMP [18]; learned: DRSN [37], MDSR [13], single-task variant of MTN (STN); ablations without axial MLP, DR Conv, attention (pp. 12-14).
metrics: NMSE of cascaded channel estimation; achievable sum-rate with the estimated channels; pilot overhead; FLOPs and parameters (pp. 12-13).
complexity: Table II: ES-MTN 1.808 GFLOPs, 1.357 M parameters (DRSN 2.756 GFLOPs, MDSR 3.729 GFLOPs); complexity orders of conv and axial MLP blocks (pp. 10-11, 13).
q1_support: p. 4: "Following the 3GPP standard in the indoor mmWave communications [25], we adopt the general clustered statistical multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) channel modeling framework". [25] is 3GPP TR 38.901 (p. 15); path loss follows the 5G mmWave Indoor Hotspot model (p. 4); near-field and visibility-region parts are custom.
q2_support: p. 14: "To present the network generalization, the MTN model is trained with the fixed HWIs". Fig. 14 tests HWI levels 0 to 0.2, an impairment-level sweep like SNR or CSI error; for pilots (Fig. 11, p. 13) the network is adjusted to each Q; no new scenario, band, or dataset is tested.
q3_support: p. 12: "A typical LS estimator is compared"; p. 12: "A multi-scale deep network (MDSR)-based channel extrapolation framework in RIS systems is extended to the STAR-RIS channel estimation". Fig. 9 (p. 12) compares NMSE of LS, CS, DRSN, MDSR and MTN; Fig. 10 (p. 13) compares sum-rate.
q4_support: p. 13: "Table II summarizes the required training overhead for DL-based channel estimation schemes". Table II (p. 13) lists ES-MTN at 1.808 GFLOPs and 1.357 M parameters, versus 2.756 and 0.821 for DRSN and 3.729 and 2.666 for MDSR.
q5_support: p. 1: "The code is available at https://github.com/WiCi-Lab/MTN".
notes: Included, area 2: cascaded channel estimation for STAR-RIS (hybrid near/far field). q1 is counted as met because the paper says its clustered channel framework follows 3GPP TR 38.901 [25] and the InH path loss, although the near-field and visibility-region parts are custom; reviewer to confirm. q2 is 0 because the only train/test mismatch is the HWI level (Fig. 14), treated as an impairment sweep like SNR or CSI error; reviewer may overturn. Dataset size and training SNR are not stated.
